definition: The compounding loop where a deployed product generates usage data, which improves the model, which improves the product, which attracts more usage.
details: The compounding loop where a deployed product generates usage data, which improves the model, which improves the product, which attracts more usage. The structural moat behind most successful applied-AI companies.

explainer.lead: A data flywheel is a feedback loop in which using an AI product creates data that can make its model better. A better model can improve the product, attract more use, and generate still more data, giving the product a potential compounding advantage.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a music player that learns which songs you skip and which ones you finish. It uses those clues to play songs you like better, so you keep using it and give it even more clues. A data flywheel is that repeating circle of use, learning, and improvement.
tiers.practitioner: Teams apply this by collecting useful interaction signals, filtering and labeling them, adding them to training or evaluation pipelines, and deploying validated model updates. Weak or biased feedback, privacy constraints, and measuring activity instead of genuine improvement can stall the loop or make the product worse.
tiers.paperLevel: The loop can be written as: product use U_t generates data D_t; D_t supports model update M_(t+1); M_(t+1) improves product P_(t+1); and P_(t+1) increases U_(t+1). Compounding depends on the data being usable and additional data continuing to improve performance; noise, selection bias, saturation, and data-use restrictions limit the effect.

explainer.example: A writing assistant suggests sentence rewrites, and users accept some suggestions while editing or rejecting others. The team uses suitable feedback to improve the model, tests that the new version produces better rewrites, and releases it; the improved assistant attracts more rewriting sessions, creating another round of feedback.

usedIn.name: Recommendation services
usedIn.detail: Interactions such as selections or skips can inform later recommendations, which shape subsequent use.

usedIn.name: AI coding assistants
usedIn.detail: Accepted, rejected, or edited suggestions can provide feedback for evaluating and improving future suggestions.

usedIn.name: Customer-support products
usedIn.detail: User ratings and corrected answers can become feedback for improving response quality.

explainer.intuition: Each cycle turns product use into an opportunity to learn, and better learning into a reason for people to use the product more. The advantage comes from the repeated loop, not from merely storing a large amount of data.
howItWorks: People use the deployed AI product.
Their interactions produce usage data or feedback.
Selected data helps evaluate or improve the model.
The improved model makes the product more useful.
Greater use produces another round of data.
explainer.whyItMatters: A working flywheel can turn early product adoption into a lasting advantage through repeated model and product improvements. It matters most when a company can collect relevant feedback lawfully, learn from it reliably, and deliver improvements that users notice.
misconceptions: More usage data does not automatically produce a better model.
Collecting data once is not a flywheel; improvement and further use must close the loop.
A flywheel is not guaranteed to be an unbeatable competitive moat.

diagram.caption: The flywheel compounds only when each link turns usage into a real product improvement.
